title: cofail: correlated failure between open language models, at the exact conditional null
description:
Code, harvested substrate, results artifacts, pre-registration, and paper for a study of correlated failure between open language models using the exact conditional null implied by Rasch sufficiency (margin-preserving randomisation / curveball). Covers 1,228-1,373 models per benchmark across five Open LLM Leaderboard v1 benchmarks (ARC-Challenge, Winogrande, TruthfulQA, GSM8K, HellaSwag), harvested at zero compute cost by column-selective parquet reads.

Mean pairwise co-failure -- the double-fault diversity measure of the classifier-ensemble literature -- is shown to be a deterministic function of item margins and therefore uninformative by construction. The exact fit-free conditional null this implies is validated (uniformity not rejected by chi-square against complete fibre enumeration; Gelman-Rubin diagnostics), power-characterised against planted alternatives including an explicit blind spot (zero power against a shared item-difficulty alternative, by construction), and applied at scale. Findings include: residual correlation surviving conditioning that is not a near-duplicate artifact (dedup-robust on 14 of 15 statistic-benchmark pairs); a negative result that diversity metrics -- classical or margin-conditioned -- add negligible incremental predictive value for panel/ensemble accuracy over member accuracy alone; and a withdrawal of the paper's own original headline claim (the participation ratio does not count 'effective independent models') after adversarial review.

Released under MIT (code) with a documented, verified upstream license chain for the derived data (see DATASHEET.md) -- ARC-Challenge is CC-BY-SA-4.0 and the corresponding derived matrices are share-alike, not MIT.
